content:
KOHRS Content Briefs -- 10 Videos Owed to Leigh

Created: 2026-03-09 Client: KOHRS Contact: Leigh Kohrs Vertical: Demolition, home renovation, design Platforms: Instagram, LinkedIn Status: Briefs ready. Waiting on footage + editing capacity.

How to Use These Briefs

Each brief is a self-contained editing assignment. When footage arrives or editing time opens up:

  1. Grab a brief
  2. Pull matching footage
  3. Edit against the structure, hook, and specs
  4. Output to projects/content-agent/output/kohrs/
  5. Mark the brief as complete

Brief 1: Demo Day Highlight Reel

Concept: Fast-paced montage of a demolition job. The visceral, satisfying destruction that stops the scroll. Let the energy of the work do the talking.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 15-25s Edit pattern: Before/After Reveal (Option B: side by side) Platform: Instagram Reels, TikTok

Hook: Open on a sledgehammer mid-swing or a wall coming down. On-screen text: "Demo Day." Body: Rapid cuts of the demolition in progress. Dust, debris, tools, crew in action. 2-second clips max. CTA: "Follow for more Demo Days." or "Tag someone who needs this energy on a Monday."

Footage needed: Raw demolition footage from any recent KOHRS job. Wide shots of the space before demo, close-ups of tools hitting surfaces, crew working, debris cleanup. Music: High energy, percussive. Match cuts to the beat. Captions: Minimal on-screen text. Let the visuals carry it.

Brief 2: Before/After Kitchen Renovation

Concept: The classic transformation. Show the kitchen at its worst, then the finished product. Same angle if possible.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 20-30s Edit pattern: Before/After Reveal (Option C: reverse reveal) Platform: Instagram Reels, TikTok

Hook: Open on the finished kitchen. Beautiful, clean, bright. Hold 3 seconds. Then: on-screen text "But when we got here..." Body: Cut to the before state. Outdated cabinets, damaged counters, old fixtures. Speed through the work in progress. CTA: "Thinking about a kitchen remodel? Start here." with @kohrs tag

Footage needed: Before photos/video of a kitchen pre-renovation. Progress shots during the work. Final beauty shots of the completed kitchen (multiple angles, good lighting). Music: Build from low/tense (before) to bright/confident (after). Beat drop on the transition. Captions: "Before" / "After" text overlays. Timeline on screen: "3 weeks."

Brief 3: Educational -- "3 Things to Check Before Hiring a Demo Crew"

Concept: Position KOHRS as the expert. Quick educational content that drives saves. Leigh as the authority voice.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 20-30s Edit pattern: Educational / Quick Tip Platform: Instagram Reels, LinkedIn

Hook: On-screen text: "3 things to check before hiring a demo crew." Bold, centered. Body:

  • #1: "Are they licensed and insured?" (visual: paperwork or KOHRS license)
  • #2: "Do they handle hazmat?" (visual: asbestos/lead testing or protective gear)
  • #3: "What's their cleanup process?" (visual: clean, swept job site post-demo)

CTA: "Save this for your next project."

Footage needed: B-roll of KOHRS crew in safety gear, clean post-demo sites, any documentation/licensing visuals. Leigh speaking to camera optional but strong. Music: Subtle, informational energy. Not distracting. Captions: Numbered steps on screen. Full text readable without sound.

Brief 4: Process Breakdown -- "How We Demo a Bathroom in One Day"

Concept: Step-by-step process of a bathroom demolition. Shows professionalism and speed. High save potential.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 25-35s Edit pattern: Process Breakdown Platform: Instagram Reels, LinkedIn

Hook: On-screen text: "How we demo a bathroom in one day." Visual: crew arriving or prepping the space. Body:

  • Step 1: Protection and prep (covering floors, taping off adjacent rooms)
  • Step 2: Fixtures out (toilet, vanity, shower)
  • Step 3: Tile and drywall removal
  • Step 4: Inspection and cleanup CTA: "This is what a professional demo looks like. Need one? Link in bio."

Footage needed: Sequential footage of a bathroom demo from start to finish. Each step needs at least one clear shot. Music: Rhythmic, building energy. Steps should hit on beats. Captions: "Step 1" / "Step 2" / etc. on screen throughout.

Brief 5: Product Video -- Tool or Material Spotlight

Concept: Highlight a specific tool or material KOHRS uses. Why they chose it, what makes it better. Short, punchy, educational.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 15-20s Edit pattern: Educational / Quick Tip Platform: Instagram Reels

Hook: Close-up of the tool/material in use. On-screen text: "The [tool] that changed how we do [task]." Body: Show it in action. What it does, why it matters. 2-3 quick clips of the tool being used on a real job. CTA: "What's your go-to [tool type]? Drop it below."

Footage needed: Close-up footage of a specific tool or material in use on a KOHRS job. Leigh or a crew member holding/using the tool. Music: Clean, modern, short loop. Captions: Tool name and use case on screen.

Brief 6: Demo Day #2 -- Slow Motion Destruction

Concept: Same Demo Day energy as Brief 1, but leaning into slow-motion for dramatic effect. The satisfying content angle.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 15-20s Edit pattern: Behind the Scenes Platform: Instagram Reels, TikTok

Hook: Slow motion of something breaking, falling, or being torn out. No text for the first 2 seconds. Let the visual hit. Body: Mix slow-mo destruction with real-speed crew work. Contrast in speed = visual interest. CTA: "This is what we do. #DemoDay"

Footage needed: Slow-motion footage of demolition (most phones shoot 240fps slo-mo). Walls coming down, tile breaking, fixtures being ripped out. Music: Heavy bass drop or dramatic orchestral hit. The slo-mo needs audio weight. Captions: Minimal. Maybe just "KOHRS" logo at the end.

Brief 7: Before/After Bathroom Renovation

Concept: Second before/after, this time bathroom focused. Different structure than Brief 2 to keep the feed varied.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 15-25s Edit pattern: Before/After Reveal (Option A: sequential) Platform: Instagram Reels, TikTok

Hook: Open on the before state. Ugly, dated bathroom. No text, no context. Let it sit for 2 seconds. Body: Text appears: "Before." Hold another 2 seconds. Hard cut on a beat drop to the finished bathroom. "After." Same angle. Pan slowly across the finished space. CTA: "14 days. Same bathroom. DM us."

Footage needed: Matching-angle before and after shots of a completed bathroom renovation. The closer the camera position matches, the stronger the impact. Music: Build tension in the before section, release on the cut to after. Captions: Just "Before" and "After" on screen. Let the visuals work.

Brief 8: Crew Culture -- Meet the KOHRS Team

Concept: Humanize the brand. Show the people behind the hammers. Builds trust and doubles as recruitment content.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 25-35s Edit pattern: Crew Culture / Team Spotlight Platform: Instagram Reels, LinkedIn

Hook: Crew member mid-action or mid-laugh. On-screen text: their name + role. Body: Show them working, then a quick candid moment (joke with the crew, something real). Cut to another crew member. Same structure. 2-3 people featured. CTA: "This is the team behind your project." LinkedIn version: "Building a crew that shows up every day. That's what it takes."

Footage needed: Candid footage of KOHRS crew on the job. Working shots mixed with real moments (lunch break, banter, high-fives after a milestone). Names needed for on-screen text. Music: Upbeat, personality-driven. Something with swagger. Captions: Name + role for each person featured.

Brief 9: Educational -- "What Happens After Demo Day"

Concept: Most people see the destruction. Show what comes next. The unsexy but critical work that makes a renovation succeed.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 20-30s Edit pattern: Educational / Quick Tip Platform: Instagram Reels, LinkedIn

Hook: On-screen text: "Everyone loves Demo Day. Nobody talks about what happens next." Body: Show the post-demo process: inspection, measurement, ordering materials, prepping for the rebuild. The organized, methodical side. CTA: "The real work starts after the dust settles. Save this."

Footage needed: Post-demolition footage: clean site, measuring, inspecting framing/plumbing/electrical, material staging, planning discussions. Music: Calmer, methodical energy. Contrast to the Demo Day chaos. Captions: Steps or process notes on screen. Educational tone.

Brief 10: Demolition Footage Compilation -- "This Week on Site"

Concept: Weekly recap format. Shows that KOHRS is constantly active, always on a job. Consistency = credibility.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 25-35s Edit pattern: Day in the Life / POV Platform: Instagram Reels, LinkedIn

Hook: On-screen text: "This week on site." Cut immediately to the first clip. Body: 6-8 clips from the week's work. Different jobs, different moments. Mix wide shots with close-ups. Include at least one crew face. CTA: "Another week in the books. What's your project?" LinkedIn version: "Consistent execution, every week. That's how trust is built."

Footage needed: Assorted clips from the current week's jobs. Doesn't need to be polished. Real, raw, active. Music: Energetic, momentum-building. Something that feels like forward motion. Captions: Day or project labels on each clip segment.

Content Mix Summary

Brief Type Platform Priority Edit Pattern
1 Demo Day Highlight IG, TikTok Before/After
2 Kitchen Before/After IG, TikTok Before/After (Reverse)
3 Educational (Hiring Tips) IG, LinkedIn Educational
4 Process Breakdown (Bathroom Demo) IG, LinkedIn Process
5 Product/Tool Spotlight IG Educational
6 Demo Day Slo-Mo IG, TikTok BTS
7 Bathroom Before/After IG, TikTok Before/After
8 Crew Culture IG, LinkedIn Crew Spotlight
9 Educational (After Demo) IG, LinkedIn Educational
10 Weekly Recap IG, LinkedIn Day in the Life

Balance: 3 educational, 3 before/after + demo day, 2 behind-the-scenes/culture, 1 process, 1 recap. Covers all algorithm signals: saves, shares, loops, watch time.

Bottleneck: Footage. These briefs are ready to go the moment raw clips land. When James is re-engaged or Patrik has editing time, grab any brief and start cutting.
